title: What is known about 1RB0LA_0RC---_1RD0LE_0LC0RE_1RF0RB_1LA1RD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LA_0RC---_1RD0LE_0LC0RE_1RF0RB_1LA1RD.
intro: This six-state machine is a holdout of the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The right side of the tape behaves like a counter in base 3/2, the numeration of Collatz-like machines; the machine halts only if state B reads a 1. No halt in the first 1011 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (B1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The sweeps of the run
claims.text: The shift rules the machine uses in its run (every sweep met when the symbolic simulator runs from many configurations of the run), each for every number of copies.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 271 cells have been visited and 118 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: A direct run of 10<sup>11</sup> steps without a halt.

claims.title: Right extensions by factors of 1.5
claims.text: From step 139,644,038 on, the busiest cell turns 285,018, 427,933, 641,487, 962,206, 1,443,670 times between consecutive right-end extensions (then the same again after a restart: 641,553, 962,401, 1,443,533, 2,165,391, ...).

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/exp
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.051). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.062).

claims.title: A base-3/2 counter
claims.text: The factor 1.5 per new cell suggests a counter in base 3/2 on the right, the numeration of Collatz-like machines.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts only if B reads a 1 (after A0 or E1); the right side looks like a base-3/2 counter, whose rules are not decoded.

claims.title: Exactly 2/3 as many visits every 3 cells
claims.text: Between steps 3·10<sup>8</sup> and 3.1·10<sup>8</sup> the busiest cell is cell 108 (201,806 turns); every third cell to its right has 134,539, 89,692, 59,794, 39,862, 26,574, 17,718, 11,813, 7,876, … turns, ratios 1.4999–1.5000, the signature of a base-3/2 counter; far left the turns halve every 4 cells (binary).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine's right side grows like a counter in base 3/2: each new cell at the right end costs one and a half times the visits of the one before, the pattern of Collatz-like machines. It halts only if state B ever reads a 1.

facts.text: No halt in a direct run.
Visits per new cell at the right end.
The sweeps of the run, proved for every length.

sections.heading: A counter in base 3/2
html: Count how often the head turns at each cell between steps 3·108 and 3.1·108. The busiest cell is cell 108 with 201,806 turns. Going right three cells at a time the counts are 134,539, 89,692, 59,794, 39,862, 26,574, 17,718, …: each exactly 2/3 of the one before. That is what a counter in base 3/2 does: every digit passes 2 carries on for every 3 it receives. Far to the left the counts halve every four cells, a binary counter.

Written as words 1…1 0 the digits right of the engine are 0, 1 or 2 ones long, and each visit of the head rewrites a prefix of variable length, so the digits do not sit at fixed cells. The exact increment rule is the next thing to decode.

sections.heading: A counter in base 3/2
html: At its right-end visits the right part of the tape is a word in 10, 110 and 1110, with a fixed tail. Each time the head extends the tape on the right, the busiest cell has turned about 1.5 times as often as the time before: 285,018, 427,933, 641,487, 962,206, 1,443,670 between consecutive right-end extensions from step 139,644,038 on (and the same pattern again after each restart). That is the signature of a counter in base 3/2, where adding to the lowest digit carries upward with a factor 3/2: the kind of numeration behind Collatz-like machines such as Antihydra.

sections.heading: A slower, irregular side
html: The left side grows far more slowly and irregularly (the busiest cell turns 202,215, 1,789,546, 4,800,410, 8,534,372 times between left-end extensions at steps 21,310,616, 126,868,352, 364,736,478, 899,271,976), and after each left-end visit the right side starts its pattern of factors 1.5 again. The rule linking the two is not decoded.

sections.heading: The halting transition
html: The machine halts only in state B reading a 1. B is entered from A0 (1RB) and E1 (0RB), used 9·107 and 2·107 times in 109 steps, and every time the next cell was a 0. There is no rare transition to watch; halting needs A> 0 1 or E> 1 1, a pattern the run's words never produce so far.

sections.heading: What would settle it
html: Find the digit values of the words 10, 110, 1110 and the carry rule of the right counter, and what a left-end visit does to it. If it is a base-3/2 counter fed by the left side, the halting question is likely a Collatz-like question about the parities met by repeated multiplication by 3/2.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.051). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.062).
After 109 steps the tape spans 271 cells (33 left of the start, 223 right), with a density of 1s of 0.435.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: The right side grows like a counter in base 3/2 (each new cell 1.5 times the visits of the last), the left side slowly; it halts only if B reads a 1 (family H, Collatz-like candidate).
